verdict_a_acceptance.reason: The observer now reads the offscreen CDP session before the first send, retains HTTP status and a bounded structured error code, and refuses transport proof when either attempt has no status. Native first-send status/code and the reporter's first guest error remain unverified. A target whose attachedToTarget initial URL is empty and later becomes offscreen.html is resumed without Network.enable, so its first request is missed.
evidence: tests/browser/guest-chat-store-acceptance.mjs arms opening before submitQuestion and requires both attempt statuses before transport proof
tests/browser/guest-chat-transport-observer.mjs:66-82 classifies only the initial attachedToTarget URL and has no targetInfoChanged listener

Inline EventEmitter reproduction: attachedToTarget URL empty, targetInfoChanged URL offscreen.html, then POST/402 events -> snapshot []; requireGuestTransport throws opening_guest_ai_transport_unobserved

verdict_b_quality_privacy_cleanup.quality: Important: optional Network.getResponseBody rejection is caught locally, while vault-owned-cdp.cjs treats any CDP protocol error as a fatal shared-connection failure. Body unavailable/evicted on an HTTP error can poison later acceptance commands and bury the HTTP status. The test double resolves getResponseBody and does not cover this failure. The source-order sequence test is a change detector, not a behavioral proof.
verdict_b_quality_privacy_cleanup.privacy: PASS for the new observer's persisted request fields: attempt, UTC time, browser-local CDP request ID, status, and syntax-restricted code only. Request URL, headers, body and response body are not retained by the observer. This does not assess pre-existing report diagnostics.
verdict_b_quality_privacy_cleanup.cleanup: PARTIAL: stop resumes tracked paused targets, disables auto-attach, removes listeners and detaches existing session on the normal path. Existing-session detach failure is swallowed by attachTargetSession in the harness, so stop cannot truthfully detect that cleanup failure. No native cleanup run was performed.
